name: Raman Monitoring of S. cerevisiae Bioreactor Fermentations (Klaverdijk et al. 2025)
description: Inline Raman monitoring of S. cerevisiae batch and fed-batch bioreactor fermentations for 3-target regression of process variables (Glucose [mM], Ethanol [mM], Biomass [g/L]): 65 in-line measurements from 5 fermentations -- 3 batch cultivations used as the paper's calibration set (B1: 12, B2: 13, B3: 13 samples), 1 unseen batch cultivation for validation (B4: 13), and 1 fed-batch cultivation for transfer testing (FB: 14). Kaiser Raman RXN2 analyzer with a 785 nm laser and a fiber-optic bIO-Optic immersion probe mounted through the bioreactor head plate; each measurement is a single 60 s acquisition (the deposit also holds 2/4/6/8/10-min stackings of the same 60 s blocks, which are excluded here; the paper calibrated all models on the 1-min spectra). 100-3,425 cm^-1 at 1 cm^-1 (3,326 points; one common grid for all samples). group_ids are the 5 fermentations (B1, B2, B3, B4, FB): samples of one cultivation are strongly correlated time points of the same process and must not be split across train/test (leave-one-batch-out is the paper's validation protocol). 5 glucose reference values (HPLC) failed in the base set and are NaN; all other 190 target values are complete. Spectra are raw instrument output as deposited (strong fluorescence background, no baseline correction or normalization). The same 4TU deposit's other chapters hold single-compound, synthetic, and augmented spectra for transfer-learning studies.

rai:dataCollection: Raman spectra were acquired experimentally using a laser spectrometer. Each spectrum represents the scattered light intensity as a function of Raman shift (cm⁻¹).
rai:dataCollectionType: Laboratory measurements on biological materials including microorganisms, cell cultures, fermentation broths, and plant material.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Spectra may have undergone baseline correction, smoothing, normalisation, and wavenumber calibration. Exact steps are described in the accompanying publication.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground-truth target values measured by validated reference analytical methods (e.g., enzymatic assays, dynamic light scattering, gas chromatography, or DFT computation).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All spectra originate from chemical, biological, or material samples without individual human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Data were acquired under controlled laboratory conditions and may not generalise to field or clinical settings. Spectral profiles are influenced by instrument-specific factors (laser wavelength, detector type, optical path length, integration time). Class imbalances may be present in classification datasets.
rai:dataLimitations: Spectral signatures are process- and instrument-specific; calibration transfer to other setups requires additional validation.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables the development of rapid, inline bioprocess monitoring tools that can reduce waste, improve yield, and lower costs in biomanufacturing and biotechnology.
rai:dataUseCases: Chemometric modelling, calibration transfer, multivariate regression, quantitative spectral analysis, process analytical technology (PAT).
